key_insight: The paper shows that parametrizing the Hamiltonian of an Interactive Quantum Classifier gives a closed-form Fourier description of the model output, where input features map to constant, sine, and cosine terms.
engineering_relevance: This provides a principled way to design quantum feature maps with controllable frequency structure, including non-separable encodings that may improve classification on nonlinear problems.
method: Derived an analytical reduced quantum channel for a single-target-qubit IQC.
Interpreted Hamiltonian parameters as coefficients shaping Fourier components of the classifier output.
Extended the encoding to matrix-parameterized environmental Hamiltonians for richer feature interactions.
evidence_signal: Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets showed improved performance on several nonlinear benchmarks, with the matrix-parameterized encoding performing best overall and a simpler four-parameter variant often close behind.
watch_item: Higher expressibility did not reliably predict better classification accuracy, so model design and task fit matter more than state complexity alone.
paper_title: Fourier Analysis of Parametrized Interactive Quantum Classifiers
